title: bridge-shift-daybook
content:
Purpose and scope:
Small personal daybook for transitions when I'm bridging shifts (evening->day, weekend->weekday). Not intended as canonical runbook yet — quick fixes and temporary mitigations I actually use. Keep messy.

Quick context (TL;DR):
- When latency spikes/queueing increases: usually CPU saturation on autoscaler pod or backing redis queue backlog.
- Frequent culprit since Nov 2025: nightly load tests hitting batcher with long seq lengths, KV cache thrash.
- This doc is for my handover + ephemeral mitigations while we finalize the proper runbook in Confluence.

Shift start checklist (first 10 min):
- Check PagerDuty queue: any unack? (pd list --service Redwood-Oncall)
- Open Grafana dashboards: Service: inference-runtime / Batcher / KV-cache. Look at 5m and 1h trends.
- Query recent errors: kubectl -n infra logs deploy/inference-proxy --since=1h | grep -i error
- Check cluster autoscaler events: kubectl get events -n infra --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 50
- Slack quick ping: #sre-oncall "On shift: Ava (bridge). Alerts in last hour?"

Immediate triage quick flow (first 30 min):
1) Is the service fully down or degraded?
   - Down: follow final escalation matrix (see below) and declare P1.
   - Degraded (high 95p latency, some errors): check batcher queue depth + pod CPU.
2) Reproduce/confirm with curl against staging/health endpoint and a lightweight generation test (use short seq length) to confirm control plane vs heavy real requests.
3) If queue depth > 5000 and batcher pods at 95% CPU: increase batcher replicas (temporary)
   - kubectl scale deploy/batcher --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy batcher -o jsonpath='{.status.replicas}')+2)) -n infra
   - Note: scaling is temporary — open SRE-412 followup.
4) If KV cache miss rate spikes: restart cache nodes one-by-one to avoid cold miss storm.

Temporary mitigations I actually used (do and log):
- Route high-cost requests to fallback model variant (cheaper small-model) via routing override in console: route override -> model=redwood-compact-v2 -> applies to 1h window. Log in incidents channel.
- Short-term rate-limit by API key: update token quota in internal dashboard for suspect key.
- Disable nightly load-test job in infra-ci: Jenkins -> disable job "nightly-inference-smoke" (only if impact is high and out-of-hours).

Sample commands stash (copy/paste friendly):
- Check pods sorted by CPU: kubectl top pods -n infra --sort-by=cpu | head -n 20
- Batcher pod logs tail: kubectl logs deploy/batcher -n infra -c batcher --tail=200
- Restart single cache node: kubectl rollout restart statefulset/kv-cache -n infra --field-selector metadata.name=kv-cache-2

Escalation quick matrix (who to @):
- Level 1 (SRE oncall): @maya (Maya Chen) — slack: @maya — pager duty SRE-L1
- Level 2 (Serving runtime lead): @liam (Liam Patel) — call: +1-XXX-555-0198 — if not available, escalate to @jordan
- Product infra owner (for routing/sla/business sign-off): product-alerts@redwood.ai (email)

What to write in the handoff message (short template):
- Summary: brief one-line (what happened now)
- Actions taken: bulleted, with timestamps (UTC)
- Current state: stable/degraded/down + next action planned
- Who's next: name + contact (this is you if you stay on)
- TODOs for followup ticket: list
Example: "Summary: Increased 95p latency for /generate from 350ms->1.6s between 03:10-03:37 UTC. Actions: scaled batcher +2 replicas at 03:15, routed heavy-model traffic to compact at 03:22. Current state: 95p back to 420ms but error rate still 0.2%. Next: open SRE-412 followup to tune autoscaler. Next shift: Jordan Kim (slack @jordan)."

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Autoscaler config: target CPU vs custom metric? We need to test target 65% vs 50% under mixed seq-len workload. (Ticket: SRE-420).
- Cache restart sequencing: documented procedure in Confluence is vague; write step-by-step after next planned restart.
- Should we add a short-lived circuit-breaker in proxy for long-seq token-limited requests? Prototype idea in PR #987 but not merged.

Runbook draft outline (for Confluence copy later) — very rough:
- Purpose and scope
- Pre-shift checklist
- Detection: metrics and alert definitions (with grafana links)
- Immediate triage steps (triage flow)
- Containment actions (scale, route, rate-limit)
- Recovery steps (pod-level, cfg rollbacks)
- Postmortem and followups
- Communication templates

Personal TODOs (short):
- [ ] Move this doc into Confluence under SRE runbooks as an editable page (Ava)
- [ ] Add explicit kubectl commands for safe cache restart (pair with Jordan)
- [ ] Create a dashboard panel for batcher queue saturation (low priority)
- [ ] Confirm phone escalation list is up to date with People Ops

Known recurring items (historical snippets):
- Nov 2025: batching thrash due to nightly long-priming tests -> mitigation was routing to compact model (worked but increased error for certain clients).
- Jan 2026: autoscaler misconfiguration caused pods not to scale above 6; fixed by adjusting HPA target CPU metric.

Quick sign-off template for leaving shift (message I actually paste in slack):
"Leaving shift — state: STABLE (95p latency Xms). Actions done: scaled batcher +2, routed heavy model -> compact, opened SRE-412 for followup. Next oncall: @Jordan. Ping if anything flares; I will check async until 22:00 PST"

Version notes:
- v0.1: started 2025-11-02 as private scratchpad.
- v0.3: added escalation matrix and command stash 2026-03-10.

Random notes-to-self: write more automation to detect repeated routes to fallback model (signal for capacity investments). Also coffee.

End of daybook entry. Keep it messy.
